title: AI search statistics and research findings
author: Josh Blyskal
readingRule: Keep each value with its sample, unit, period, and caveat. The studies use different corpora and must not be pooled.

findings.finding: Generative requests were the largest classified ChatGPT prompt-intent category.
findings.sample: Classified sample drawn from more than 50 million prompts; classified sample size unpublished
findings.caveat: The unit is prompts, not unique users, and follow-up turns are included.

findings.finding: The tested traditional SEO metrics explained a small share of citation variance.
findings.caveat: The observational association was statistically reliable at p<0.001 but does not establish causation.

findings.finding: Blogs, opinion pages, comparisons, and listicles supplied most classified citations.
findings.caveat: This is citation composition, not the probability that a page of each type will be cited.

findings.finding: The most frequently shown product pages contained more FAQs and videos than the least shown group.
findings.caveat: The comparison is descriptive and does not establish that either feature caused visibility.

findings.finding: Claude citations also appeared in Brave positions one through ten.
findings.caveat: The observed match does not prove that Brave directly caused Claude's source selection.

findings.finding: Claude and ChatGPT shared few citation domains on average.
findings.caveat: The public materials do not report the overlap formula, collection window, or per-engine citation counts.

findings.finding: Reddit ranked first among cited domains in the pooled answer-engine dataset.
findings.sample: More than 4 billion citations and 300 million responses
findings.caveat: The pooled result masks engine differences, including a number 31 rank on Microsoft Copilot.

findings.finding: Four-to-seven-word natural-language slugs were more common in the highly cited group.
findings.sample: 50,000 highly cited URLs compared with 50,000 low-cited URLs
findings.caveat: Group prevalence does not show that changing a URL causes citation growth.
